source_observations.finding: The original _safe_file formed (root/raw).resolve() before candidate.is_symlink(). As an isolated helper this loses lexical symlink identity when a link resolves to an in-root regular file.
evaluate_portable_release_static_completeness composes evaluate_pre_handoff_release first; that path calls load_and_verify_release_manifest before the WP1111 metadata reference checks.

Release-manifest construction/verification walks the entire payload with followlinks=false and fail-closes on any symlink directory or symlink file before exact payload comparison. Therefore an ordinary symlink substitution in the package is rejected upstream of WP1111 _safe_file.

Existing release-integrity tests already assert that a symlink file is rejected by the canonical manifest builder. Source also rejects symlink directories, although this exact directory case is not separately asserted in that test file.
Trigger-4 added lexical component walking and symlink rejection to WP1111 as defense-in-depth after this E1 claim was acquired.
Trigger-4 added final-file and intermediate-directory symlink regressions to the WP1111 full evaluator.
The new WP1111 adversarial-symlink regression run completed FAILURE in the fail-closed component suite. This is negative evidence; no acceptance credit is granted.

external_primary_sources.finding: Path.resolve() makes a path absolute while resolving symlinks; is_symlink() answers whether the path being queried is itself a symbolic link. This supports the isolated-helper critique that resolve-before-link-inspection can erase lexical link identity.

Python 3.14 defaults tar extraction to the data filter, documents symlink-driven later-member hazards, and explicitly recommends disallowing symbolic links when not needed. It also warns that filters do not protect against live destination mutation.

openat2 provides path-resolution constraints including RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS and RESOLVE_BENEATH/RESOLVE_IN_ROOT for kernel-enforced traversal boundaries. This is relevant only if F2 later needs live untrusted filesystem access; it is not required to prove a frozen static release manifest.

The Go os.Root design explicitly notes that resolve-then-validate schemes can be TOCTOU-racy and uses root-relative traversal-resistant operations on supported systems. This supports keeping static lexical validation distinct from runtime filesystem confinement.

hypotheses.statement: The original WP1111 resolve-before-is_symlink order creates a reachable release-root confinement bypass in the composed static completeness evaluator.
hypotheses.reason: The canonical release-integrity layer verifies the whole payload first and rejects symlink files/directories before WP1111 metadata reference validation.

hypotheses.statement: The original _safe_file ordering is locally unsound but redundant/unreachable for ordinary symlink substitution under the current composed evaluator; remaining risk is helper reuse outside the manifest gate or a live mutation race between validation and later use.

evidence_boundary.note: E1 source reading plus CI observation only. No E2/E3/E4/E5/E6 promotion is minted here.
